trust_decision.summary: Whether a configured Terraform Cloud / registry bearer token may be attached to a request whose host comes from scanned input (cloud/backend `hostname`, remote-run URL, tfr:// module source). At the pinned commit no host comparison exists anywhere; the token goes to whatever host the input names.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Terraform Cloud token ... via unvalidated hostname'. The only place where a .tf `hostname` attribute repoints the authed client is Load's SetHost(config.Host).

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: internal/providers/terraform/terragrunt_hcl_provider.go:137-140 (wired tgterraform.RegistryGetter from the gruntwork-io/terragrunt dependency) and internal/providers/terraform/terragrunt_registry_service.go:253-264 (local copy that the fix adopts); a different token (TG_TF_REGISTRY_TOKEN) and a different transport (go-getter tfr://)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The registry path uses TG_TF_REGISTRY_TOKEN, a Terragrunt-documented env var, not the Terraform Cloud token from the report, and the live getter sits in a third-party dependency (tgterraform.RegistryGetter), so a solver can argue it is upstream Terragrunt behaviour outside Infracost's TFC hostname bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate tokens must keep flowing: (1) when no primary TERRAFORM_CLOUD_TOKEN is set, a host-scoped token from ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json / TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE for a non-default TFE host must still be used; (2) TFE users who pin TERRAFORM_CLOUD_HOST must still get remote vars and remote plans; (3) registry tokens must still reach registry.terraform.io, app.terraform.io private registry, the configured TFE host and TG_TF_DEFAULT_REGISTRY_HOST; (4) an explicitly configured org/workspace (TERRAFORM_CLOUD_ORG/WORKSPACE) uses the trusted host. Over-broad fixes (always drop the token on any hostname, refuse whenever host differs even with no primary token, never use the .tf hostname) break these.

O6_input_shapes: hostname in terraform { cloud { hostname = ... } } block
hostname in terraform { backend "remote" { hostname = ... } } block (workspaces name or prefix)
host parsed from the terraform CLI remote-run URL in stdout
registry host from a tfr:// module source, plus an empty host defaulting to TG_TF_DEFAULT_REGISTRY_HOST
registry host from an absolute modules.v1 base path returned by service discovery (checked per request)
case variants and trailing-dot variants of the trusted host (hostsEqual: EqualFold + TrimSuffix ".")
trusted host configured explicitly vs. defaulted to app.terraform.io (warn-and-skip vs. hard error)

O7_producer.where: internal/hcl/modules/credentials_source.go:47-50 defaults an empty TerraformCloudHost (internal/config/config.go:106-108, env TERRAFORM_CLOUD_HOST) to app.terraform.io before the loader is built, so the loader cannot tell a configured host from a defaulted one. The fix threads hostConfigured from hcl_provider.go to parser.go to the loader. The untrusted host itself is produced by the HCL block mapper at internal/hcl/remote_variables_loader.go:273-326.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The second TFC API call in the remote-plan path joins a response-supplied json-output path onto the host as `https://host+path`, so a path starting with '@' would move the bearer token to another host. The fix validates the host but leaves this path unchecked.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: jsonPath comes from the (now validated) trusted TFC server's JSON response, not from the scanned Terraform, so it is 'trusted server output'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as a fix site; sink in internal/providers/terraform/cloud.go:17-23

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ForHost falls back to the base TERRAFORM_CLOUD_TOKEN for any registry host when no host-scoped credential is found (module-registry route into the same token)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer could add it as a convenience so private-registry modules work with only TERRAFORM_CLOUD_TOKEN set. It sits in internal/hcl/modules, far from the report, and reaches registry.go:162/279 PrepareRequest.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a terraform_remote_state / backend "remote" outputs or state fetcher that reads config.hostname and calls the authed client without the hostsEqual check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same block-parsing mapper and the same AuthedAPIClient. Fetching remote state for cost references is a plausible feature next to remote variables.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cloudAPI building the URL by string concat with a path from a response (userinfo '@' or '//' host differential)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already the shape at dir_provider.go:455. Making the parser differential HOW-type needs only a host-joining helper used by a second caller.
